title: Discomfort with assessment of probing pocket depths at endosseous implants depending on the width of the keratinized/attached mucosa/gingiva
summary: Periodontal and peri-implant probing may cause discomfort/pain. Earlier studies have shown that peri-implant probing causes more discomfort/pain than periodontal probing in general. Discomfort/pain during periodontal/peri-implant probing may be influenced by several factors (e.g., inflammation of tissues). Also the width of the keratinized/attached mucosa around implants may have an effect. This study was set up to show whether the width of the keratinized/attached mucosa around implants has an effect.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Patients with an endosseous implant and a contralateral tooth. Contralateral means the same jaw and tooth type (anterior tooth, posterior). 
•	Patients must be able to understand the documents presented.
•	Patients must accept the study conditions.
•	The age of the patients must be 18 years or older.
Exclusion criteria:
•	Iodine allergy
•	Taking medications that have an effect on bone remodeling or soft tissue healing (e.g., steroids, bisphosphonates)
•	Minors
